title: Keyword Documentation - Explaining Your Tools
description: Document your keywords using [Documentation] setting for better maintainability.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, a tool without instructions is hard to use. The [Documentation] setting explains what a keyword does, its arguments, and what it returns."
story.context: Documentation appears in test reports and helps other robots (or your future self) understand how to use keywords correctly.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! Your keyword is now self-documenting. Anyone reading the report will know exactly what it does!"

instructions: Create test 'Documented Check' that calls: Verify System Health    sensors
Add [Documentation] as FIRST line: Checks if specified system is healthy and operational
hints: [Documentation] must be FIRST line in keyword
Documentation is a string explaining the keyword
Shows up in test reports and IDE tooltips
solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Documented Check
    Verify System Health    sensors

*** Keywords ***
Verify System Health
    [Documentation]    Checks if specified system is healthy and operational
    [Arguments]    ${system_name}
    Log    Verifying ${system_name} health
    Log    ${system_name} is healthy

theory.title: Exercise 2.2.5: Keyword Documentation
theory.content:
📚 Tools with Instructions

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, imagine finding a complex tool with no manual. You'd have to guess how it works! Documentation prevents that."

"The [Documentation] setting explains: What does this keyword do? What arguments does it need? What does it return?"

📝 What is Keyword Documentation?

[Documentation] - Metadata that describes a keyword's purpose and usage

  • ✅ Clarity - Explains what the keyword does
  • ✅ Usage guide - Shows how to call it correctly
  • ✅ Maintenance - Helps future developers understand code
  • ✅ Reports - Appears in test execution reports

Benefits:

  • 🔹 IDE tooltips show documentation when hovering
  • 🔹 Test reports include keyword descriptions
  • 🔹 Team members understand keywords without reading code
  • 🔹 Generated documentation from test files

📝 Documentation Syntax

*** Keywords ***
Login To System
    [Documentation]    Logs into the system using provided credentials.
    ...                Returns True if login succeeds, False otherwise.
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    # Keyword implementation
    RETURN    True

Simple Keyword
    [Documentation]    Does a simple operation
    Log    Simple operation

Multi-line Documentation:

Complex Keyword
    [Documentation]    This keyword performs multiple steps:
    ...                1. Initializes the system
    ...                2. Validates input
    ...                3. Returns status code
    [Arguments]    ${input}
    # Implementation

📋 Documentation Rules

  • 🔹 Position: FIRST line in keyword (before [Arguments])
  • 🔹 Syntax: [Documentation] Description text
  • 🔹 Multi-line: Use ... for continuation
  • 🔹 Order: [Documentation] → [Arguments] → keyword body
  • 🔹 Best practice: Document all public keywords

🎯 Your Task

Create a keyword with both [Documentation] and [Arguments]. The documentation should explain what the keyword does!
